name: Mercury
fact: The smallest planet is also the fastest: Mercury completes an orbit in just 88 Earth days. Its path is distinctly elliptical.

name: Venus
fact: Venus takes 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun, but 243 Earth days to rotate once. Its rotation runs opposite to Earth’s.

name: Earth
fact: Earth completes one trip around the Sun in about 365.25 days. Its average distance from the Sun defines the familiar one-AU comparison.

name: Mars
fact: A Martian year lasts 687 Earth days. Mars has seasons like Earth, but its elliptical orbit makes their lengths uneven.

name: Jupiter
fact: Jupiter needs about 12 Earth years for one orbit. The largest planet is roughly 11 times wider than Earth, yet spins once in only 9.9 hours.

name: Saturn
fact: Saturn takes about 29.4 Earth years to circle the Sun. Its rings are made of countless pieces of ice and rock, each orbiting the planet.

name: Uranus
fact: Uranus completes an orbit in about 84 Earth years. Its 97.77° axial tilt makes it appear to roll on its side as it travels around the Sun.

name: Neptune
fact: Neptune takes about 165 Earth years to orbit the Sun. In 2011, it completed its first full orbit since its discovery in 1846.
